question: Let $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & a & a^2 \\ 1 & b & b^2 \\ 1 & c & c^2\end{array}\right| = 0$. Prove that at least two among $a, b, c$ are equal.
explanation:
This is a Vandermonde determinant:

$|(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)|$

If the determinant is zero, at least two of $a, b, c$ must coincide.

Hence, at least two are equal.

options.A: The determinant is always zero for all values of $a,b,c$, so no relation among $a,b,c$ is needed.
options.B: The determinant is a Vandermonde determinant equal to $(b-a)(c-a)(c-b)$. Since it is zero, at least one factor is zero, so at least two among $a,b,c$ are equal.
options.C: The determinant is equal to $a+b+c$. Since it is zero, $a+b+c=0$, so all three numbers are equal.
options.D: The determinant is equal to $abc$. Since it is zero, one of $a,b,c$ must be zero, but no two values are equal.
